doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Heifetz's verdict on Joe Venuti
summary: Gallodoro tells how Jascha Heifetz told Venuti he could have been a great concert violinist, citing his intonation on the album.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I wanted to say. Joe Venuti is on there. I think you know the story. Many years ago, Jascha Heifetz went to hear Joe Venuti play. And Jascha told Venuti, he says, “if you had gone in to be a concert violinist, you would have been one of the greatest.” Because he had the time and he had the intonation. You notice about Joe? You have the record. He does “How High the Moon,” and he does “Autumn Leaves.” His intonation is beautiful.
I think he did okay staying in the jazz field, don’t you?
